<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="BRPXQZME" />{{running header|384|{{asc|THE SHIH KING.}}|{{smaller|{{asc|DECADE I.}}}}}}{{rule}}</noinclude>He called his Superintendent of Works;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He called his Minister of Instruction;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And charged them with the rearing of the houses.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
With the line they made everything straight;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
They bound the frame-boards tight, so that they should rise regularly:{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Uprose the ancestral temple in its solemn grandeur<ref>This stanza describes the preparations and processes for erecting the buildings of the new city. The whole took place under the direction of two officers, in whom we have the germ probably of the Six Heads of the Boards or Departments, whose functions are described in the {{tooltip|Shû|Shū}} and the [[Rites of Zhou|Official Book of ''K''âu]]. The materials of the buildings were [[w:Rammed earth|earth and lime pounded together in frames]], as is still to be seen in many parts of the country. The first great building taken in hand was the [[w:Ancestral temple|ancestral temple]]. [[w:King Tai of Zhou|Than-fû]] would make a home for the spirits of his fathers, before he made one for himself. However imperfectly directed, the religious feeling asserted the supremacy which it ought to possess.</ref>.

Crowds brought the earth in baskets;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
They threw it with shouts into the frames;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
They beat it with responsive blows.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
They pared the walls repeatedly, till they sounded strong.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Five thousand cubits of them arose together,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
So that the roll of the great drums did not overpower (the noise of the builders)<ref>The bustle and order of the building all over the city is here graphically set forth.</ref>.

They reared the outer gate (of the palace),{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Which rose in lofty state.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
They set up the gate of audience,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Which rose severe and exact.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
They reared the great altar to the spirits of the land,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
From which all great movements should proceed<ref name="418_3">[[w:King Tai of Zhou|Than-fû]] was now at leisure to build the palace for himself, which appears to have been not a very large building, though the Chinese names of its gates are those belonging to the two which</ref>.
